note: Family B of the parity run's behavioural diff: React's World3dHost mounts one BrushMeshRegistrar per loaded GLB per window instance and announces its welded collision geometry to the puzzle guest; the wgpu host dispatched nothing at all, so the guest's brush and volume-brush utilities had no collision body on this renderer. Every React row below is `origin: gesture` on the scene host's own controller — never `user` — which is the provenance the wgpu twin stamps too (`dispatch_gesture_action`).

announce.note: An identity the client's registry already holds under THIS guest instantiation — because a sibling window paged it, or a sibling id carries byte-identical geometry — costs one command and no payload. React's `handleRegisterBrushMesh` holds/alias fast paths.

page.note: One page of a first upload: base64 of little-endian f32 positions followed by little-endian u32 indices, positions filling each page first and the indices stream continuing in whatever of the page's value budget is left. The guest reassembles it in `decode_brush_mesh_page_values` and refuses a run that does not hash to the announced digest.

digest.over: positions little-endian f32 bytes followed by indices little-endian u32 bytes
digest.note: Byte-identical to the guest's own `brush_mesh_digest` (`✏️editor/⏳️precompute/🦀️.rs`) and React's `puzzle3dBrushMeshDigest`.

laws.perWindowInstance: Every one of the seven measured steps carries rows for BOTH window instances — an announcement is scoped to a window, never to the document, because React mounts a registrar per World3dHost. The wgpu twin therefore keeps its announced set per `World3dState`.
laws.oneRowPerIdentityPerRevision: A surface announces an identity once per registry revision and never twice in the same frame. React's registrar re-fires on its `revision` prop, which is `brushMeshRevisions.generation + brushMeshRevisions.urls[url]`; the wgpu twin reads the same two numbers off the guest's own `interactionJson.meshResidency` / `interactionJson.meshReuploadUrls`.
laws.reannounceTriggers: A window that is rebuilt (window-reopen, role-viewer, role-editor) starts with an empty announced set and announces again; an example switch changes the mesh url set and announces the new identities; a guest restart (meshResidency going backwards) voids every claim and bumps the revision for all of them.
laws.backPressure: At most ONE command is outstanding per surface while a first upload runs, so a user action that lands mid-run queues behind a single page rather than behind a whole 72-command run (React's `drainPuzzle3dBrushMeshQueue` awaits each page's settle; the wgpu twin emits one page per surface per frame).
laws.sharedRegistry: The claim ledger is process-wide, exactly as React's `puzzle3dBrushMeshRegistry` is a module singleton shared by every mounted host: the first window pages the bytes, and every later window announces the same identity by `{url, digest}` alone.
